name: Cordouan Lighthouse
description: Cordouan Lighthouse stands on a small rocky plateau in the Atlantic, about 7 kilometres off the French coast at the mouth of the Gironde estuary. Begun in 1584 and finished in 1611, it is France's oldest lighthouse. Its 67.5-metre white limestone tower is richly carved with columns, pilasters and gargoyles, so it looks more like a Renaissance palace rising from the waves than a plain beacon. It still guides ships today.
